cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Culinary – (adjective) related to cooking or the kitchen.

p.em: Example: Remy possesses an extraordinary culinary talent that surpasses human chefs.

cosy-blockquote.p: Scavenge – (verb) search for and collect anything usable from discarded waste.

p.em: Example: The rat colony is content to scavenge garbage, but Remy craves gourmet flavors.

cosy-blockquote.p: Gourmet – (adjective/noun) involving high-quality, refined food.

p.em: Example: Remy dreams of preparing gourmet French dishes inside Paris's finest restaurants.

cosy-blockquote.p: Authenticity – (noun) the quality of being real, genuine, or true to one's passion.

p.em: Example: Chef Gusteau's recipes celebrate authenticity and passion over rigid rules.

cosy-blockquote.p: Connoisseur – (noun) an expert judge in matters of taste or fine art.

p.em: Example: Anton Ego prides himself on being the ultimate connoisseur of Parisian dining.

cosy-blockquote.p: Prestige – (noun) widespread respect and admiration felt for someone or something based on achievements.

p.em: Example: Gusteau's restaurant struggles to regain its lost prestige after losing a star.

cosy-blockquote.p: Recipe – (noun) a set of instructions for preparing a particular dish.

p.em: Example: Linguini stumbles through the kitchen until Remy guides his movements according to the recipe.

cosy-blockquote.p: Prejudice – (noun) preconceived opinion that is not based on reason or actual experience.

p.em: Example: Remy must overcome human prejudice against rats to pursue his dream.

cosy-blockquote.p: Epiphany – (noun) a moment of sudden and profound revelation.

p.em: Example: Taking his first bite of ratatouille triggers a childhood epiphany for Anton Ego.

cosy-blockquote.p: Hierarchy – (noun) a system in which members of an organization are ranked according to relative status.

p.em: Example: Colette explains the strict kitchen hierarchy of sous-chefs, line cooks, and dishwashers.

cosy-blockquote.p: Anyone can cook – (phrase) Chef Gusteau's famous motto celebrating universal artistic potential.

p.em: Example: 'Anyone can cook' inspires Remy to believe that great art can come from anywhere.

cosy-blockquote.p: Little chef – (noun) Linguini's affectionate nickname for Remy hiding under his hat.

p.em: Example: Linguini relies completely on his 'little chef' to survive in the high-pressure kitchen.

cosy-blockquote.p: Gusteau's legacy – (noun) the culinary philosophy and recipes left behind by Auguste Gusteau.

p.em: Example: Skinner attempts to commercialize Gusteau's legacy with cheap frozen microwave meals.

cosy-blockquote.p: Kitchen hierarchy – (noun) the traditional French brigade system organizing kitchen roles.

p.em: Example: Colette teaches Linguini how to respect the fast-paced kitchen hierarchy.

cosy-blockquote.p: Anton Ego – (noun) the feared food critic whose reviews can make or break a restaurant.

p.em: Example: Anton Ego enters Gusteau's with cold arrogance, demanding to be challenged.

cosy-blockquote.p: Garbage rat – (noun) Django's pragmatic view of rat identity in human society.

p.em: Example: Django warns Remy that humans view rats as nothing more than disease-carrying garbage rats.

cosy-blockquote.p: Ratatouille dish – (noun) a traditional Provençal stewed vegetable dish.

p.em: Example: Remy serves a modest peasant ratatouille dish to the most terrifying critic in France.

cosy-blockquote.p: A taste of home – (phrase) food that evokes nostalgic memories of childhood warmth.

p.em: Example: The simple vegetables give Anton Ego an unforgettable taste of home.

cosy-blockquote.p: Ego's review – (noun) the legendary newspaper column that restores Gusteau's reputation.

p.em: Example: Ego's review declares that a great artist can come from the most humble origins.

cosy-blockquote.p: La Ratatouille – (noun) the cozy bistro opened by Remy, Linguini, and Colette at the end.

p.em: Example: La Ratatouille features a special miniature dining room created exclusively for rats.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
Remy refuses to eat garbage like his colony, insisting on pairing fine cheese with fresh strawberries. How does his refined palate set him apart from his family?
★ What is a passion or interest you have that makes you feel different from those around you?

Chef Auguste Gusteau appears as a helpful figment of Remy's imagination. How does this inner mentor guide Remy when he feels hopeless in Paris?
★ How do mentors : real or remembered : help us stay true to our goals during difficult moments?

Linguini has zero cooking skills but inherits Gusteau's restaurant. How does his partnership with Remy under the chef's hat create chaotic harmony?
★ Why do unexpected partnerships between people with different skills often produce great results?

Colette Tatou is the only female cook in Gusteau's kitchen, working twice as hard to earn respect. What does her character reveal about perseverance?
★ How can standing up for your worth in a competitive environment inspire others?

Chef Skinner tries to profit off Gusteau's image by selling frozen microwavable meals. How does his greed contrast with true culinary art?
★ What happens to art or food when commercial profit becomes more important than quality?

Django takes Remy to a pest control shop window filled with dead traps to warn him about humans. How does Remy respond to his father's fear?
★ How should young people balance listening to parental warnings with pursuing their own dreams?

Linguini gets overwhelmed by sudden fame and temporarily takes credit for Remy's genius. How does vanity test their friendship?
★ What should you do when a friend or colleague takes credit for work you accomplished together?

When the health inspector arrives, the entire rat colony steps up to wash, cook, and serve food under Remy's direction. How thrilling is this climax?
★ How does seeing a marginalized group unite to achieve something incredible inspire audiences?

Remy serves Anton Ego a simple peasant dish : ratatouille : instead of an elaborate luxury meal. Why is this choice a brilliant artistic risk?
★ Why can simplicity and genuine emotion often impress critics more than complex luxury?

Anton Ego loses his job and status as a top critic after praising a rat-staffed kitchen, but he becomes a happy investor in La Ratatouille. Is this true success?
★ How can letting go of arrogance and status lead to genuine personal happiness?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative task or visual analysis in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: Collaborative task or visual study.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: 1-on-1 guided visual description and task response with teacher.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Look at the prompt and discuss your response with your teacher:

cosy-blockquote.p: Collaborative task or visual study.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
Director Brad Bird used glowing color bursts and synchronized music to represent flavor combinations on screen. How effective is this visual metaphor?
★ How can cinema convey invisible sensory experiences like taste or smell through visual art?

Pixar animators took cooking classes and studied real rotting produce to render food texture accurately. How does attention to detail elevate animation?
★ How does realistic detail in animated food or environments make a movie more immersive?

Paris is depicted with golden romantic lighting, rainy cobblestone streets, and warm kitchen glow. How does the setting become its own character?
★ What movie location or city made you fall in love with its atmosphere just by watching it?

Anton Ego's office is shaped like a coffin and his typewriter resembles a skull. How does exaggerated visual design communicate character traits?
★ How do set designers use gothic or ominous visual shapes to tell you about a villain's mindset?

The flashback scene where young Ego drops his bicycle and receives a bowl of stew from his mother lasts only seconds. Why is it so emotionally powerful?
★ What specific food or dish instantly transports you back to a warm childhood memory?

The film explores the tension between tradition (rigid French recipes) and innovation (Remy's creative combinations). Where do you stand?
★ Is it better to strictly follow established traditions or constantly experiment with new ideas?

Michael Giacchino's accordion-driven musical score captures the essence of Parisian bistro culture. How does music set the geographic tone?
★ How does a well-crafted musical soundtrack enhance your emotional connection to a country's culture?

The ending rejects a traditional Hollywood cliché where Remy magically turns human or wins public fame, keeping him a secret chef. Do you prefer this realism?
★ Why is an honest, modest happy ending often more satisfying than an unrealistic grand triumph?

Anton Ego's final review concludes: 'Not everyone can become a great artist, but a great artist can come from anywhere.' How profound is this thesis?
★ What does the phrase 'a great artist can come from anywhere' mean to you in modern society?

If you were hired to cook a single three-course meal that represented your life story and heritage, what dishes would you serve?
★ What three dishes would you prepare to introduce someone to your personal background and taste?

ul.li: Incorrect: I will resign if they skimp always on budget → Correct: I will resign if they always skimp on budget (Frequency adverbs like 'always' come before the main verb.)
Incorrect: We are living here since two years → Correct: We have been living here for two years (Use present perfect continuous with 'for' to express duration.)
Incorrect: They don't allow her leave the house → Correct: They don't allow her to leave the house (Use 'allow someone to do something' construction.)
